advances: This exact allocation transition is for the seven actual positive fibers under the two specified shape and mass cases.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The base hull is the quadrilateral $-1\le z_1\le1$, $z_2\le1$, $z_1+2z_2\ge-1$. At integer first coordinates $-1,0,1$ the allowed integer second coordinates are respectively $(0,1),(0,1),(-1,0,1)$. The added bases $(-1,0),(-1,1),(1,-1)$ uniquely maximize respectively $-2z_1-z_2,-z_1+z_2,z_1-2z_2$ on these generators. Their fibers are exactly $R,A,A$. Each core fiber stays $T$ because all continuous generators lie in $T$. The lifted core spans full dimension, and summing the seven volumes gives the stated mass.

Take a nonvertical through-cap at $((0,0),g)$, with unit continuous normal $u$. If it takes all of $R$, the shifts in the two $A$ fibers are opposite about the centroid $g$. Fact 6a7d56e450b3126f gives combined mass at least $2\Gamma_d a$ in the homothetic case. Symmetry gives combined mass exactly $a$ in the symmetric case. Together with the own cap, this gives the target. If it fails to take all of $R$, write $B=u\cdot g$ and $\ell=\min_T u\cdot x$. The threshold in $R$ exceeds $\ell$. The opposite core fiber at $(1,0)$ then has threshold less than $2B-\ell$. The own and opposite simplex captures alone have mass at least $(\Gamma_d+\rho_d)V$ by the reflected profile, which suffices. A vertical through-cap has at least the own volume $V>(\Gamma_d+\rho_d)V$. Moving a containing cap parallel inward proves the bound for all containing caps.

For each barycentric coordinate $\lambda_i$ on $T$ use the closed cap
$$
\lambda_i(x)-\frac{d}{d+1}(z_1+z_2)\ge\frac1{d+1}.
$$
Its mass is $\Gamma_d V+w+\theta a$. It fully captures $R$. At the two $A$ fibers it cuts canonical centroid caps of fraction $\Gamma_d$ in the homothetic case and $1/2$ in the symmetric case. At the adjacent core fibers the threshold is one, and at $(1,1)$ it exceeds one. The own cap has volume $\Gamma_d V$. These caps cover the whole $(0,0)$ fiber. At a noncentroid point some own barycentric coordinate exceeds $1/(d+1)$. Raise the corresponding threshold to that coordinate to strictly decrease the own mass without increasing any other trace.

At the anchors $(0,1)$ and $(1,0)$ their respective $A$ and opposite core form an actual placed three-fiber subset of the type in 98603e266680b22d. Restrict any containing halfspace to the affine base line of the triple. It gives a containing cap or the whole triple, and in either case the mass is at least $\Gamma_d V+a$ at the anchor centroid. For the matching upper covers use the affine functions $z_1+2(1-z_2)$ and $1-z_1+z_2$ at the respective anchors. Each vanishes at its anchor, is $-1$ at its owned $A$, and is at least one on every other base in the seven-site census. Subtract twice this function from $\lambda_i(x)$ and take threshold $1/(d+1)$ for all $i$. The caps take just the owned $A$ and the corresponding own cap. At a noncentroid mark raise the threshold as above to obtain a strict decrease. At $(1,1)$ the function $2-z_1-z_2$ gives the cover isolating canonical caps of mass $\Gamma_d V$. Exposed vertical cuts at the added bases have masses $w$ or $a$, both below $\Gamma_d V$ by the assumed bounds and $\rho_d<\Gamma_d$. All other points are therefore strictly below the stated global maximum, with exactly the comparisons in the statement.
statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $T$ be a $d$-simplex of volume $V$ with centroid $g$. Place $T$ at the four binary bases in two integer dimensions. Place any convex body $R\subseteq T$ of volume $w>0$ at $(-1,0)$, and the same convex body $A\subseteq T$ of volume $a>0$ at $(-1,1)$ and $(1,-1)$. Suppose either $A$ is a positive homothet of $T$ about $g$ and $\theta=2\Gamma_d$, or $A$ is centrally symmetric about $g$ and $\theta=1$. Here $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, and $\rho_d$ is the reflected simplex profile minimum of fact 53fe12b742a7608d. Assume $a\le\rho_d V$ and $w+\theta a\le\rho_d V$.

The convex hull has exactly the seven assigned integer fibers, total mixed volume $4V+w+2a$, and raw depth $\Gamma_d V+w+\theta a$ at $((0,0),g)$. Over its actual mixed-integer points the raw maximum is $\Gamma_d V+\max(a,w+\theta a)$. The maximizing set consists of $((0,0),g)$ if $w+\theta a>a$, of $((0,1),g)$ and $((1,0),g)$ if $w+\theta a<a$, and of all three at equality.
title: Exact global depth for seven fibers with a partial-trace transition
